review: 1:1–2 בְּשׂוֹרָה לָנוּ … כִּי אֱלֹהִים אֲהֵבָנוּ — the Arabic بُشْرَى لَنَا … فَاللّهُ قَدْ أَحَبَّنَا is the gospel-announcement form of Isa 52:7 (מְבַשֵּׂר … טוֹב); בְּשׂוֹרָה is the noun of that verse, so the opening cry is the herald's word and not a general 'good news'.

1:3–4 הַבֵּן בָּא אֶל־אַרְצֵנוּ … מֵת כָּאן — the Arabic وَالاِبْنُ وَافَى أَرْضَنَا … مَاتَ هُنَا لِأَجْلِنَا is 1 Tim 3:16 (נִגְלָה בַבָּשָׂר); the Hebrew keeps the coming-to-our-land and the dying-here as two separate clauses, since the Arabic's point is that the incarnation was local.

2:4 וְכָל־אֲשֶׁר־לוֹ לָנוּ — the Arabic وَكُلُّ مَا لَهُ لَنَا is Rom 8:32 (אֵיךְ לֹא־יִתֵּן לָנוּ גַּם־אֶת־הַכֹּל); the Hebrew keeps the bare 'all that is His' without adding a verb, so the line stays a statement of ownership transferred rather than a promise of giving.

3:1 מִי יִתֵּן וְנִסְתַּפֵּק — the Arabic يَا حَبَّذَا لَوْ نَكْتَفِي is a wish ('would that we content ourselves'); מִי־יִתֵּן is the biblical wish-formula (Deut 5:26, מִי־יִתֵּן), and the Niphal of ספק gives the 'be satisfied' sense of the Arabic's نَكْتَفِي.

5:1–2 יִתַּמּוּ … וְהַמִּלְחָמָה תִּכְלֶה — the Arabic أَتْعَابُنَا سَتَنْتَهِي وَالْحَرْبُ … لَا تَعُود is Rev 21:4 (וָמָוֶת … לֹא יִהְיֶה־עוֹד) with Isa 2:4; the Hebrew keeps 'toils' as עָמָל (Gen 3:17) and war as מִלְחָמָה, so the stanza closes the curse of Eden and the last battle in one couplet.
